t.E472a.agn: In 2020 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E472a.body: During digestion in the body it is largely broken down into glycerol, fatty acids and the corresponding organic acid (acetic acid); these are used like the fats in foods.
t.E472a.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E472a.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by re-esterification of fats with triacetin or by reaction of mono- and diglycerides with acetic anhydride.
t.E472a.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern.
t.E472a.regx.1: Specifications follow-up opinion: changes to the EU specifications recommended for E472a.
t.E472a.summary: An emulsifier derived from mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids. It improves texture in bread, cake and margarine; the fat source may be vegetable or animal.
t.E472a.what: As an emulsifier and coating agent, it improves structure and consistency.
